verdict: One active Facebook campaign, no visible lead outcomes — reporting gaps make performance impossible to grade this period.
diagnosis: Spend totaled $2,330 across 28 days on one Facebook lead campaign, but no lead volume or conversion data is available to judge return.

signals.headline: Total spend hit $2,330 this period
signals.detail: All budget flowed through a single Facebook campaign targeting PCOS and postpartum personas.

signals.headline: Daily spend averaged $13.63
signals.detail: Modest and steady pacing for a boutique studio testing a niche persona angle.

signals.headline: Latest day dropped to $3.85
signals.detail: Sharp pullback from the average suggests pacing throttle, budget cap, or auction weakness worth checking.

signals.headline: Zero data across 4 sources
signals.detail: No lead volume, no organic, no Google profile, no pipeline — the reporting stack is not connected.

signals.headline: One campaign carrying 100% of spend
signals.detail: Single persona and single channel means no comparison set to learn what actually works.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.body: Boutique and premium studios on Facebook typically pay $25–$50 per lead, versus $8–$15 for budget gyms. Fitness leads convert at roughly 14%, the highest of any industry tracked.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.subheader: July ad costs at yearly peak
seasonal.body: Facebook impression costs for fitness peaked at $29.68 per thousand in July 2026, the highest of the past 13 months. Summer competition is elevated; a Q4 lull typically follows.

competitor.label: Competitor
competitor.subheader: Studios shifting from acquisition to retention
competitor.body: Studio cancellations fell 6% last year while big-box gyms rose 8%. Category leaders are leaning into community, speed-to-lead follow-up, and niche positioning rather than broad paid acquisition.

recommendations.title: Connect lead tracking before adding budget
recommendations.detail: Consider wiring Facebook leads into the CRM and reporting stack. Without lead counts and cost per lead visible, the current $2,330 spend cannot be judged good or bad.

recommendations.title: Test a second creative angle against PCOS/postpartum
recommendations.detail: Worth exploring a second persona or offer angle in parallel. One campaign gives no read on whether the niche is the ceiling or the creative is.

recommendations.title: Tighten speed-to-lead follow-up under five minutes
recommendations.detail: Leads contacted within five minutes convert nine times more often than those contacted after an hour. A simple SMS auto-reply captures most of that gain.
